title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: (61) as transcribed has a spurious factor; from the previous page A+2νC=εR and C=εT give A=ε(R−2νT)=ε(R−(μ−1)T). The '2ν' and 'C' written underneath are alternative notations (2ν=μ−1), not a quotient.
The crossed-out dimension count (relative dimension 3) is wrong, as Grothendieck himself notes ('non, il est de dim. rel 4'): the equations of (61)/(62) are dependent given C+D−B=1 and AD−BC=1.
Sign inconsistency between pages: here D is expressed through c²+d²+cd, on the next page D=δ(c²+d²−cd). Harmless, since the two forms are equivalent under d↦−d, but it should be noted.
The 'theorem' is essentially a restatement of (58),(59). Determination of μ by η is only up to the sign ε, so μ is determined by η only up to sign unless ε is otherwise known.

ideas.what: Multiplier μ (cyclotomic character) of an automorphism of profinite SL2 recovered from an entry of the conjugating matrix: μD=1, μU=ε
ideas.modern_name: Cyclotomic character in Galois/GT action on the profinite modular group (inertia at elliptic points j=0,1728)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (GT and genus 0/1 Galois actions, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the Teichmüller tower and SL2(Ẑ) actions; not this computation

ideas.what: Parametrisation of matrix entries by Eisenstein and Gaussian norm forms (c²+d²+cd, t²+u²), arising from centralisers of order-3 and order-4 elements
ideas.modern_name: Unit groups of Z[ζ3], Z[i] as centralisers of elliptic elements in SL2

ideas.what: Signs ε=ε₂(μ), δ=ε₃(μ) together encoding μ mod 12 (completed on next page)
ideas.modern_name: Abelianisation SL2(Z)^ab=Z/12 and cyclotomic character mod 12

ideas.what: Scheme over Spec Z of solutions to the compatibility equations, its relative dimension, and its Ẑ-points
ideas.modern_name: Moduli scheme of solutions to the GT-type relations for SL2

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes viewing the compatibility conditions as a scheme over Spec Z of relative dimension 4 (after correction), and studying its Ẑ-points, to parametrise solutions of the 'loop equation' for SL2(Ẑ). The idea is abandoned (crossed out).
missed.quote: le schéma (sur Spec Z) des solutions de ces équations est de dimension relative 3 ... non, il est de dim. rel 4
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an explicit algebraic-geometric model of a GT-type solution set for the modular group. It is analogous to the GT and GRT group schemes but for genus one/SL2 data. Its structure does not seem to have been studied in this form, though the content is likely subsumed by later work on GT actions in genus 1.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit computation within Grothendieck's study of Galois/GT actions on profinite SL2: the multiplier is recovered from matrix entries, and parity/mod-3 signs fix μ mod 12. It is consistent with known structure. The only slightly unusual element is the abandoned idea of a solution scheme over Spec Z.
transcription_corrections: 'A=ε(R−[...](μ−1)/2ν · T/C)' should read A=ε(R−(μ−1)T), with '2ν' and 'C' written below as alternative notations.
'AB alors deux mains A conséquence des autres' is better read as roughly 'A, B alors déterminés, conséquence des autres, compte tenu de C+D−B=1 et AD−BC=1'.
The left-margin note reads 'conséquence des précédentes' and applies to the last relation(s) of (62).
The margin note reads 'non, il est de dim. rel 4'.
In (62) the third line reads ac+bd+ad−(c²+d²+cd)=δε(rt+su), with corrections visible in the image.
'On a donc une pointe [?] celle [?] de ce schéma absolu' is uncertain; the word is possibly 'partie' or 'pointe'.
